title: Fix mergeCloudPayload treating a non-empty remote payload with a missing/unparseable updated_at as unconditionally newer than local
rule: EH-2 / Nygard lens (LWW ordering must not silently clobber on ambiguous input; mirrors FB-3's null-timestamp guard even though this path is SharedPreferences-based, not core/sync)
why: The short-circuit `remoteUpdatedAt != null && ...` means: when the remote payload is non-empty but its 'updated_at' fails to parse (missing key, malformed string, cross-version format drift), the early-return guard never fires, so the method falls through and unconditionally overwrites local milestones/unlocks with the remote payload -- treating 'timestamp unknown' as 'always newer' instead of the safer 'cannot prove newer, keep local'. This is the exact malformed-timestamp branch never exercised by either reward_milestone_service_test.dart's mergeCloudPayload group (only null/empty/older/newer-with-valid-ISO-dates are tested) or test/sync/merge/gamification_reward_merge_test.dart (same gap, confirmed by grep -- only valid ISO8601 updated_at values appear in that file too).
recommendation: Change the guard so a null/unparseable remoteUpdatedAt is treated as NOT provably newer (skip the merge, same as the older-timestamp branch) rather than falling through to an unconditional overwrite.
acceptance_criteria: mergeCloudPayload with a non-empty milestones/unlocks payload and a missing or garbage 'updated_at' leaves existing local data untouched
A new test in the mergeCloudPayload group covers this exact case and fails against the current code

corrections: Minor: claim that gamification_reward_merge_test.dart has 'only valid ISO8601 updated_at values' is imprecise -- that file never exercises mergeCloudPayload at all (uses a fake callback stub), so reward_settings.updated_at never appears there in any form. Strengthens rather than weakens the zero-coverage claim.
